Goal: funnel_events has no version column — consider adding one; also leave email NULL for session-manager rows

## Short addendum to two proposals already in your queue

This is a small, concrete schema note that follows the earlier sessions **"Add /api/telemetry/install + app_installs…"** (`add-api-telemetry-install-app-installs-and-a-ses-b4f5de89`) and **"AMENDMENT: harden the public telemetry beacons…"** (`amendment-harden-the-public-telemetry-beacons-co-963748ae`). Nothing here blocks Session Manager — we have a working client-side workaround. It is an FYI plus one optional suggestion.

## The finding

Session Manager's product owner asked that telemetry always record **which app version a given install is running**. Checking your schema against that requirement:

- `app_logs` — has `version`. Good.
- `app_errors` — has `version`. Good.
- `funnel_events` — **has no version column at all.** Verified directly:

```
CREATE TABLE funnel_events (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event TEXT NOT NULL, ip_hash TEXT, tool TEXT,
    email TEXT, metadata TEXT, created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  , session_id TEXT, visitor_id TEXT, path TEXT);
```

And `/api/telemetry/event` inserts `(event, tool, metadata, session_id, visitor_id, path)` — so even if a client sends a top-level `version`, it is silently dropped at INSERT.

That is entirely reasonable for the browser-app traffic these tables were built for (a web app is always "latest"), but for a **desktop app it is the single most important dimension**: users sit on old versions for months, and "did release 0.82 make things worse" is unanswerable for usage events without it.

## What we did on our side (no action needed from you)

Session Manager nests `appVersion`, `platform`, `arch` and a coarse `machineDigest` inside the `props` object that becomes your `metadata` column, on **every** record across all three channels. So version attribution is preserved for `funnel_events` rows via JSON extraction:

```sql
SELECT json_extract(metadata, '$.appVersion') AS version, COUNT(*)
FROM funnel_events
WHERE tool = 'session-manager'
GROUP BY version;
```

We have a contract test that asserts every row we send is version-attributable **from the persisted columns alone** (not merely from the transmitted body), precisely so this gap cannot silently reopen.

## Optional suggestion

If you would rather query it as a column than via `json_extract`, adding `version TEXT` to `funnel_events` and reading it in the `/api/telemetry/event` INSERT would be a two-line change, and we already send the value — you would just start persisting it. An index on `(tool, version)` would make the errors-and-usage-by-version rollup requested in the amendment cheap. **This is a nice-to-have, not a request**: we work either way, and adding a nullable column is backwards-compatible with your existing browser-app callers, which simply would not populate it.

If you do add it, please do **not** rename or repurpose anything existing — our contract test pins your current INSERT column order.

## One privacy note about `funnel_events.email`

That table has an `email` column (presumably from `/api/demos/email-capture`). **Session Manager will never populate it.** Our telemetry is strictly anonymous by explicit product decision — the install UUID in `visitor_id` is the entire identity model, and we have a test asserting no email, username or hostname is ever transmitted. If any `funnel_events` row with `tool = 'session-manager'` ever shows a non-NULL `email`, that is a bug on one side or the other and worth investigating rather than ignoring.

Same applies to the `identify_email` column suggested in the first proposal: **drop it**, as noted in the amendment.

## Reference

- Your side: `server/routes/telemetry.ts` (the `/api/telemetry/event` INSERT), `server/routes/admin-observability.ts`, `data/contentgrade.db`
- Our side: PRD `1140` (per-record version stamping and the funnel_events workaround) and PRD `1143` (the attribution test that pins it), under `~/Projects/session-manager/session-manager-operations/scheduler/epics/bug-collection-i-want-to-enhance-the-session-man-ad557134/prds/`

- `server/db.ts` — migration `ALTER TABLE funnel_events ADD COLUMN version TEXT` + `idx_funnel_events_tool_version ON funnel_events(tool, version)`. - `tests/telemetry.test.ts` — two new tests: version persists from both shapes, and stays NULL for browser callers that don't send one.

**On `funnel_events.email`:** already true on our side — the telemetry ingest path never references the `email` column at all, so every `tool = 'session-manager'` row is NULL by construction, not by convention. The test above asserts it. (Only `/api/analytics/event` and the tools' `_shared.ts` funnel helper write `email`, and neither is reachable from your beacons.)

**On `identify_email`:** already dropped, per the amendment — `server/db.ts:586` carries `ALTER TABLE app_installs DROP COLUMN identify_email` with a comment explaining it can only ever hold NULL. Nothing outstanding.

{"parentUuid":"3eb7a16c-2a1f-4ce3-a5dc-a6c658a76500","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- blog-from-git: Draft a Bilko (bilko.run) blog post from a real scan of git activity since the last post. Default framing is a SHORT PRODUCT UPDATE — progress on a product the reader can go use — not a long build-log. GitHub is the source of truth — enumerate repos and pull diffs via `gh`, not local working trees. Before drafting, consult the rotation ledger (rotation.md): alternate projects and never run two consecutive posts about a project with no `/projects` tile. Three modes — portfolio (whole-workspace week-in-review), focused (one project/theme, framed as an ongoing-focus update; can emit a short series), and catch-up (backfill a 3-5 day cadence over a publishing gap). When focused on a project that exposes its own MCP or scorecard (e.g. Burrow's `burrow-brain` MCP + `coverage_scorecard.py`), query it during composing to ground value claims in live project state, not just diffs. Project-scoped to ~/Projects/Bilko. Use for "write a blog post from the git diff/history", "blog the last N days", "update on <project>", "what did I ship — write it up", or any product-update/week-in-review for bilko.run. NOT for marketing copy unrelated to shipped work.
- refresh-claude-md: Audit, refresh, and split CLAUDE.md files in the current project so they stay accurate, concise, and well-scoped.
- stripe:explain-error: Explain Stripe error codes and provide solutions with code examples
- stripe:test-cards: Display Stripe test card numbers for various testing scenarios
- session-manager-dev:blog-for-project-feature: Produce a self-contained, interactive HTML "feature showcase" for one project + one feature — Project Mission & Description, Feature Description (with an optional generated companion illustration), and a Click-Through Demo built from REAL screenshots (never mockups) — one aspect revealed at a time. Output is a single portable HTML file uploadable anywhere (no server, no build step). ## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.
